beats.en: Kabaddi requires no equipment: a 13×10 m court (men) or 12×8 m (women). A raider holds one breath chanting 'kabaddi, kabaddi' (called 'cant').

textbookBox.concept: Kho-Kho has 12-player squads (9 on field) and two innings of 9-minute chasing and running turns. Sitting chasers face alternate directions and can only run one way, while dodgers may run between them.

beats.en: Kho-Kho has 12-player squads (9 on field) and two innings of 9-minute chasing and running turns. Sitting chasers face alternate directions and can only run one way, while dodgers may run between them.
beats.speakEn: Kho-Kho has 12-player squads (9 on field) and two innings of 9-minute chasing and running turns. Sitting chasers face alternate directions and can only run one way, while dodgers may run between them.

beats.en: Judo ('ju' = gentle, 'do' = way) was developed in Japan using balance and leverage; three officials (1 referee, 2 judges) oversee bouts on a mat with blue and white starting tapes 4 m apart.
beats.speakEn: Judo ('ju'  equals  gentle, 'do'  equals  way) was developed in Japan using balance and leverage; three officials (1 referee, 2 judges) oversee bouts on a mat with blue and white starting tapes 4 metres apart.
